resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives 1924 (Wikidata) and 1868 (USLHS). 1868 is the first lighting, shown on 1 November 1868 per the Chapter and the Board's 1868 report as LighthouseFriends prints it. 1924 is the electrification and the end of the keeper.
The record's 'standing' (OSM) against 'lost' (LighthouseFriends, USLHS) is resolved: the 1868 brick house is gone, and a skeletal range light on the site is active.

notes_for_editor:
Leading Point: thin on keeper detail. Roster (9 lines, USLHS) is the only keeper record; no family or career detail was found in the sources read. Newspaper searches of Maryland papers for Leading Point (1866-1930) turned up only one German-language Baltimore item from 1873 and one from 1898 that were read; English-language Baltimore papers are not in Chronicling America for these years, so the 1868 lighting and the 1924 change rest on the Board's reports as LighthouseFriends prints them, the 1925 Bulletin and the Chesapeake Chapter. The Board's 1868 report is not in the local corpus (corpus lhb runs 1891-1901); the 1868 lighting is quoted through LighthouseFriends and the Chapter. The USCG Historian's Leading Point page (archived copy) returned 403 and was not read.
Corrections proposed for the record: the status says inactive, but the Directory lists the current rear range light as active; the structure 'tower, brick, built 1868, standing' conflicts with USLHS 'Torn Down 1924'. The brick structure is not standing per USLHS. The record's 'F W' characteristic matches the Chapter's 1868 fixed white only loosely (fixed white versus F W); the Directory now lists continuous green; Wikipedia's F G was not cited.
Disagreements stated in the story: whether the brick house was demolished in 1924 (Directory, USLHS, Chapter) or left standing with the new tower in front of it (Bulletin 1925). Present tower height: 55 ft in 1924 (Bulletin) against about 70 ft (Directory).
OCR: the 1891 easement passage is under the Hawkins Point heading (OCR 'ffatcJcim Point'); the story treats it as Hawkins Point. 'Arcadian' is the name as the German paper prints it (OCR reads 'Areadian' in one place and 'Arca di a' in the heading); the story keeps the spelling Arcadian. The 1873 date is mid-January: the paper of Monday 20 January names 'Friday morning' without a date.
Translation: the German quotations are checked against the OCR text; English renderings are ours.
People: the Farrow link (Leading Point 1919-1924 and Lower Cedar Point 1930-1939) is the archive's own person record, not a name match.
Not searched: photos; keepers' families in census or local papers (budget).
Fact-check 2026-10-28: corrected the second outbuilding (4 by 5 feet, not 14 by 30); placed the iron oil house in the fiscal 1897 report (not 1896); the $3,500 easement award is in the fiscal 1891 report (not the 1892 report that records the July 1891 clearing); the 1901 items are fiscal 1901; 'Day or unlighted beacons' footnoted; 1898 paper says the lights were put back in service.
